Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.
NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR REGULAR MEETING
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection at the City Library.
Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government Code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are at the Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.azusaca.gov. Persons who wish to speak in-person during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to 7:30 P.M.; cards submitted after this time will not be accepted.
Those wishing to participate during Public Comment may do so in-person at the Azusa Auditorium, or may submit written public comments by emailing PublicComment@azusaca.gov. Emailed public comments are due by 5:30 p.m. and shall be limited to no more than 250 words. Written public comments will be provided to the City Council and will be part of the record but will not be read aloud.
View the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.ci.azusa.ca.us/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website.

CITY OF AZUSA

  MINUTES OF THE CITY COUNCIL, THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY
  TO THE FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY,
  THE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  REGULAR MEETING
  MONDAY, OCTOBER 6, 2025

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in Closed and Regular session at Azusa Auditorium at 213 E.
Foothill Blvd., Azusa, CA 91702.

REGULAR SESSION

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:  GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:  NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo, City Treasurer Vasquez

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, Interim City Attorney Casso, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia,
Chief of Police Wenrick, City Clerk Services Manager Juarez, Director of Economic and Community
Development Jimenez, Community Improvement Manager Edson, Senior Community Improvement Inspector
Hale, Director of Community Resources Carpenter, City Librarian Hassen, Director of I.T. Guadagnino,
General Manager of Utilities Singh

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Adrian Martinez.

The Invocation was led by Reverend John LeRoy, First Assembly of God Church.

CEREMONIAL

1. City Council presented a letter of adjournment to the Martinez Family.

2. Mayor Pro Tem presented a Proclamation proclaiming the month of October Cybersecurity Awareness
  month in the City of Azusa.

3. City Clerk Cornejo, Chairman of the Azusa Golden Days Committee, presented the 2025 Golden Days
  Events which take place October 11–19, 2025, and presented the theme, “Día de Los Golden Days: A
  Community Celebration of Life and Heritage”; acknowledged the Golden Days Committee and all
  individuals who collaborated in planning the event; presented Councilmember Sabrina Bow with a gold
  badge; presented Robert Vargas as the Grand Marshal, George Galvez as the Civic Grand Marshal, and Joe
  Perez as the Honored Citizen for the 2025 Golden Days; and further announced the Honored Organizations
  and upcoming events.

City Council Minutes  Page | 1
October 6, 2025
 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Theresa Conley thanked Staff and the City Council for their support and direction in resolving an ongoing issue
with a business in the City.

Jenny Bolivar and Lupita Ramirez, members of the Azusa Chamber of Commerce, invited the City Council and
the community to attend the upcoming Taste of the Town event, held in celebration of Golden Days, on October
12, 2025; and reported that a community “Clicker App” is available where discounts will be posted in honor of
Golden Days 2025 using the code 286.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez reported on the very successful Azusa Night Market; noted that the only complaint
received was that the event space was too small for the number of attendees; stated that the City will continue to
build upon the event; and thanked all departments for their collaboration in hosting the event in the downtown
area.

Economic and Community Development Update

Director of Economic and Community Development Jimenez reported on recent ribbon cuttings in the City;
stated that efforts are underway to further populate the Edgewood Shopping Center with the upcoming opening
of Vallarta Supermarket on December 10, 2025; discussed several City enhancements, including holiday
decorations in the downtown area; highlighted the upcoming Classic Car Show scheduled for November 9th;
mentioned the increasing interest in recreational activities and the potential for adding new facilities; and
announced that the City is a finalist at the Eddy Awards, being recognized as an innovative,
economic-development–centric community.

Community Improvement Manager Edson provided an update on the Community Improvement Division’s
efforts to maintain and preserve neighborhoods within the City; discussed various programs administered
through the division; and highlighted special programs including the annual rental inspections, Real Property
Records Report, vacant and foreclosed property registration, and daily proactive monitoring of City graffiti,
bulky items, and shopping carts.

The Council made inquiries regarding bulky items and noted that items are still being left on front easements;
and requested that this matter be brought back to a future meeting for further discussion.

Staff reported that yellow tags are now being used on items left on easements and properties, providing
instructions on how to schedule bulky item pick-ups; stated that they are working with property managers and
owners to identify better locations for bulky item placement and to address the time frame in which items
remain out for pick-up; and reported that Community Improvement is working with Athens to obtain a list of
residents who have scheduled bulky item pick-ups.

Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez congratulated Jorge Galvez and Joe Perez on being announced as the Civic Grand
Marshal and Honored Citizen for this year’s Golden Days; commented on the success of the Night Market and
expressed interest in expanding the event to a larger area.

Councilmember Avila congratulated José Jimenez and staff for placing the City on the Eddy Award nomination
list; and expressed condolences to the family of Eddie Martinez and to Charlie Wilson and the Wilson/Carillo
family for their loss.

Councilmember Mendez noted that the Night Market received positive compliments, but it was also considered
too small and expressed support for increasing the event size; and requested that the City Manager formally
reach out to Metro to discuss a resolution regarding the exit turnstile at the Azusa Station.

Councilmember Bow reported that she attended several community events, including the 25th Anniversary
Kick-Off Party for the Azusa Renaissance Community Theater; and noted that she also attended the 70th
Anniversary Celebration for Totten Tubes, a local steel tube manufacturer.

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
October 6, 2025
 Mayor Gonzales reported that he attended the JPIA Conference and provided a brief overview of the
homelessness-related sessions presented during the conference.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

CONSIDERATION OF NOMINATION TO THE SAN GABRIEL BASIN WATER QUALITY AUTHORITY
(WQA) BOARD FOR THE REPRESENTION OF CITIES WITH PRESCRIPTIVE WATER PUMPING
RIGHTS AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 2025-C44

City Clerk Services Manager Juarez presented a resolution for consideration to nominate Mayor Gonzales to the
San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority Board as the representative for cities with water pumping rights;
noted that the nomination must be made by resolution and submitted to the Water Quality Authority no later
than October 18, 2025; and reported that Mayor Gonzales is the current member serving on the Board and that
his term is scheduled to expire on January 1, 2026.

Moved by Councilmember Bow and seconded by Councilmember Mendez and carried by the following vote of
the Council, to adopt Resolution No. 2025-C44 nominating Mayor Robert Gonzales to represent cities with
prescriptive water pumping rights on the Board of the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority.

AYES: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
NOES: NONE
ABSENT: NONE
ABSTAIN: NONE

Total Cost: N/A Is the Cost of this item budgeted? N/A
Fund/Account No: N/A

UPDATE ON SENATE BILL 1383 COMPLIANCE AND COUNCIL CONSIDERATION ON PROPOSED
FRANCHISE AGREEMENT CHANGES BY ATHENS SERVICES

Environmental Program Specialist Sagun presented an update on Senate Bill 1383; and proposed a commercial
and multi-family three-stream program transition, which includes expanding recycling participation in the
commercial sector, meeting Azusa’s procurement target, and implementing recycling programs for City special
events.

Director of Government Affairs for Athens Services Amaya, further explained the proposed commercial and
multi-family three-stream program; presented information on the previously adopted amendment and outlined
additional program elements to be implemented, including data reporting and food recovery support; described
the three-stream program noting that commercial and multi-purpose properties will receive a blue trash barrel,
similar to Azusa residents, as CalRecycle will begin requiring cities and haulers in January to divert 75% of
organic material from landfills; and stated that the proposed program is intended to help meet this requirement.

Amaya also described the “Pay-As-You-Throw” program versus “Bundled Service” options, reviewed the
proposed bundle options and rates, and mentioned that support will be provided to commercial customers
during the transition; and concluded by explaining the next steps for the City, which include a contract
amendment, municipal code update, and a Proposition 218 hearing.

The Council ensued questions regarding the proposed contract amendment, including whether there will be any
changes to residential rates; whether different bin options will be provided under the new program; whether
residents will have the option to downsize or upsize bins; and what challenges commercial customers may face
if they are unable to enclose their bins.

Staff responded that no residential rate changes will be made at this time and that different bin options will be
available for customers as needed; noted that they will work with customers to provide appropriate sizing and
material bin options; and mentioned that discussions with Code Enforcement and Building officials will be
necessary to determine how accommodations can be made for enclosed bins.

City Manager Gonzalez stated that this item will be brought back at a future meeting with a proposed
amendment for the Council’s consideration and approval.
